purpose: Decide and execute the pre-plate mechanical finish on a working gold-plating bench: set the target surface (mirror, satin or matte) that a thin conformal gold deposit will faithfully reproduce, choose the hand-abrasive, wheel, compound or tumble route that reaches it with minimum metal removal, protect detail, hallmarks, joints and thin-skinned constructions along the way, and know exactly when to stop and hand a finished, honestly documented surface to the chemical prep line.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

every piece arrives with a completed triage packet from substrate assessment: substrate class verified by test-method classes, existing coatings and previous plate recorded, solder joints and repairs flagged, stones and organics already removed or the piece refused, and any irreversibility sign-off already countersigned

abrasives, compounds, media and burnishing soaps are purchased commercial products used per their maker's technical data sheet; compound families (tripoli-class cutting bars, rouge-class coloring bars, greaseless satin compounds) are named as trade classes, never as recipes or setpoints

thickness figures for electroplate classes and clad shells are cited as handbook-class or marking-rule-class ranges from the grounding corpus, never as guarantees; marking terms such as gold plated, vermeil, gold filled and rolled gold plate are regulated classes and current rules must be verified in the operator's jurisdiction

safety at the polishing station is stated as obligation classes (guarding, dust extraction, eye protection, work-holding rules, training, metal-bearing-waste routing) and the operator must verify their jurisdiction's workplace and hazardous-waste rules; local disposal rules for polishing waste are treated as unknown until checked
exclusions: substrate identification and piece triage: base-metal family determination, hallmark reading and interpretation, test-method classes (magnet, weight and feel, spot test), porosity and repair assessment, and the accept/refuse/refer decision - that is the substrate-assessment KB's territory; this KB consumes its verdict and never re-litigates it

all wet chemistry from polished to plate-ready: soak and ultrasonic degrease, electrocleaning, activation and pickle, the water-break test, rinse cascade design, no-touch handling and time limits to tank entry - that is the chemical-prep KB's territory; this KB only defines what condition it hands over and what the traveler must disclose

chemical stripping of existing plate and any improvised chemistry whatsoever; prep chemicals are commercial products used per their TDS, and on any line holding both cyanide and acid products their segregation (storage, use, drains) is absolute - mechanical finishing never touches or relaxes that boundary

stone-set, pearl or organic, antique, filled or repaired pieces that triage flagged for refusal, stone removal or referral - such a piece never reaches a wheel here, however profitable the job; a customer piece is never risked to keep work in-house

irreversible mechanical work performed without explicit documented customer sign-off: deliberately cutting through existing plate, softening engraved detail, or removing hallmarks - the sign-off is created at triage intake and this KB only verifies and obeys it
plating-bath operation, deposit thickness selection, post-plate finishing and topcoats, and all selling or marking claims about the finished article - downstream specialists own those decisions

competency_questions.question: What must be in my hands from triage before any abrasive or wheel touches a customer piece, and what stops the job cold?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer lists the triage packet contents (verified substrate class, coating and joint flags, stone and organic clearance, refusal and referral verdicts, countersigned irreversibility sign-off where needed) and names missing sign-off or a refuse/refer verdict as absolute stops

competency_questions.question: Why is the customer's final finish made at my bench rather than in the tank, and how do I turn a customer expectation into a bench-usable target finish spec?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states that decorative gold electroplate is thin and conformal so it reproduces the pre-plate surface nearly unchanged, and shows a finish spec naming mirror/satin/matte, texture direction, and a reference sample when matching existing work

competency_questions.question: How does each base-metal class I meet (brass, copper, zinc die-cast, silver, mild steel, stainless, previously plated work) behave under abrasives and wheels, and what does that change in my plan?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer gives behavior-at-the-wheel differences (cut rate, smearing and loading, detail blur, work-hardening, heat sensitivity, thin-coating risk) and ties each to a concrete plan change such as lighter compound, backed hand work, or tumble routing

competency_questions.question: How do I set a metal-removal budget for a specific piece before starting, and what enforces the stop when the budget is reached?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer derives the budget from what is thinnest and irreplaceable (existing plate class, clad skin, wall thickness, crisp detail) before work starts, and names the stop discipline: agreed defects only, disclose what the budget cannot fix, never polish to taste on customer goods

competency_questions.question: How do I map and classify a piece's defects before finishing, and which defects get removed, reduced, or left and disclosed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer describes magnified raking-light inspection producing a written defect map where every scratch, pit, dent and worn zone carries a remove/reduce/disclose class agreed before work begins

competency_questions.question: When do deep defects call for graded hand abrasives before any wheel, and what goes wrong if I skip grades or jump straight to the buff?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer explains that each abrasive grade exists only to remove the previous grade's scratches, that skipped grades telegraph through color work and plate, and that buffing a deep scratch instead of sanding it dishes a bright hollow around it

competency_questions.question: How do I choose compound families per stage and substrate, and how does the shop guarantee a coloring wheel never carries cutting grit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer matches compound class to stage and metal per the compound maker's guidance and states the dedication regime: one wheel one compound for its whole life, labeled, raked, stored apart, retired on suspicion

competency_questions.question: How do I keep crisp edges, milgrain, engraving and hallmarks alive at the wheel, and what may never be polished away without paperwork?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer names the seconds-fast blur mechanism of a mop over detail, gives protection tactics (masking, thumb shielding, felt sticks and hand work near marks), and states that hallmark removal or detail softening requires the documented customer sign-off from triage

competency_questions.question: When does a piece go to tumble or media finishing instead of the wheel, and which media class does what to the surface?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer routes chains and flexible link goods away from the wheel unconditionally, weighs batch economy against per-piece control, and distinguishes steel-shot burnishing (moves metal, near-zero removal) from abrasive ceramic or plastic media (removes metal) and magnetic-pin overuse (peened texture)

competency_questions.question: How do I produce a specified satin or matte target, or match an existing texture on a partial refinish, and where in the sequence does texturing sit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer places texture as the last mechanical step over an already-leveled surface, names direction and grade matching against a reference coupon, and explains why a stray color pass after texturing forces rework

competency_questions.question: What are the special rules when gold-filled, rolled-gold or antique gilt goods reach the finishing bench, including suspected fire-gilt ormolu?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states burnish-do-not-abrade for clad skins whose microns are the product, requires sign-off before any abrasive touches them, and refuses mechanical refinishing of suspected fire-gilt antiques outright because residual mercury is a recognized conservation-class hazard

competency_questions.question: What safety obligation classes govern the polishing station, and where does gold-bearing or lead-suspect polishing dust go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer covers eye protection, dust extraction and respiratory protection classes, the no-chains no-gloves no-loose-clothing rules at a spinning wheel, work-holding position, jurisdiction verification, and routing of metal-bearing sweeps to a refiner rather than the trash

competency_questions.question: What must pass at the finish QC gate before a piece leaves mechanical finishing, and what must the chemical prep line be told at handoff?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer lists the gate checks (spec match under raking light, no coarse scratches beneath the finish, detail and hallmarks intact, photographs for customer goods) and the traveler contents (compound family used, flagged zones such as solder smear risk, prompt routing before residue hardens)

competency_questions.question: Mid-cut I uncover something the plan did not include - a pit that keeps opening, worn plate breaking through, or grey smear near a repair joint. What do I do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer is stop, photograph, and re-contact rather than improvise: porosity-connected pits are not chased, deliberate cut-through of old plate needs the sign-off, and low-melt solder smear is contained by hand-finishing around the joint and flagging the zone

glossary.definition: The metal-removing buffing stage: firmer wheels charged with a cutting-class compound level scratches and refine the surface left by hand abrasives; it is where nearly all buffing metal loss happens, so the removal budget lives or dies here.

The final luster stage: soft loose-sewn mops with a coloring-class compound bring the leveled surface to full brightness with very little removal; it cannot fix scratches, only make whatever is there shinier.

Grease-bar or greaseless abrasive product charged onto a wheel; trade classes include tripoli-class cutting bars, rouge-class coloring bars and greaseless satin compounds - purchased products applied per the maker's guidance, never mixed or improvised.

The shop law that a buffing wheel carries exactly one compound for its entire life, is labeled with it, is raked to renew its face, and is stored away from other compounds; it is the only reliable defense against cross-contamination scratching.

Low-angle light swept across a surface under magnification; it throws shadows from scratches, pits, dents and texture breaks that overhead light hides, and is the standard inspection method at defect mapping and the finish QC gate.

Glossing by plastic deformation - hardened steel shot or a polished tool rubs the surface and moves metal instead of removing it; the correct finishing class for microns-thin gold skins and the mechanism of steel-shot tumbling.

The reappearance of an under-surface defect through everything applied over it: a skipped abrasive grade, an unremoved coarse scratch or an opened pore shows straight through color work and through a thin conformal gold deposit.

Clad construction classes: a wrought karat-gold skin roll-bonded to a base core at the mill, marked by weight fraction under marking-rule classes; the skin is finite and cannot be restored at the bench, so abrasive finishing spends the product itself.

The historical mercury-amalgam gilding process, prohibited today; antique fire-gilt objects can retain residual mercury, so mechanically refinishing or heating them is a recognized conservation-class hazard and such work is refused and referred.

glossary.term: flash / gold plated / heavy gold plate
glossary.definition: Electroplate thickness marking classes referenced from the grounding corpus: flash-class deposits are hundredths-to-tenths of a micron, the gold-plated class sits near half a micron, and heavy-gold-plate and vermeil classes sit at the few-micron threshold - classes to verify in your jurisdiction, and all thin enough that the pre-plate finish shows through.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for gold_plating_mechanical_finishing work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Verify the substrate-assessment handoff before any mechanical work: the traveler must state the verified substrate class, existing coatings and previous plate, solder joints and repair zones, confirmation that stones, pearls and organics are off the piece or the piece was refused, and - for any planned irreversible act - the customer's countersigned sign-off created at triage. The finisher's job here is enforcement, not re-assessment: a missing field, a refuse or refer verdict, or an absent sign-off stops the job before the first abrasive pass, because the wheel converts triage mistakes into permanent damage in seconds.

included: escalation back to triage on gaps
excluded: creating a sign-off at the bench

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a quarter of bench-incident logs showing which traveler fields actually predicted damage would re-rank or extend this gate's checklist

pros.claim: A five-minute packet check is the cheapest insurance in the shop because it catches irreversible mistakes while they are still free
pros.example: spotting that a ring flagged pot-metal-with-lead-solder-repair has no repair-zone note on the traveler, before a buff smears grey solder across the shank

cons.claim: Strict enforcement stalls easy jobs when triage paperwork lags the physical piece
cons.example: a plain brass cigarette case waits a day for a countersignature although nothing about it is risky, and the customer chases the delay

failure_modes: starting wheel work from memory of a verbal triage summary and missing a flagged repair zone
treating the packet check as a formality and not opening the sign-off page
quietly proceeding on a piece triage marked refer because the defect looks trivial at the bench
acceptance_tests: no job enters mechanical finishing without a traveler stating substrate class, coating and joint flags, stone and organic clearance, and sign-off status
a deliberately incomplete test traveler is stopped at intake and routed back to triage, not worked
revisit_triggers: a bench incident traces to a field the packet check does not currently require
triage changes its packet format or adds a new verdict class

nodes.definition: Translate the customer-agreed final appearance into a bench-usable pre-plate finish specification, on the principle the whole subdomain rests on: decorative gold electroplate is thin and conformal, so the tank reproduces the surface it is given - mirror in, mirror out; scratches in, gold-plated scratches out. The spec names the finish class (mirror, satin, matte), the texture direction and grade for non-mirror targets, which faces carry which finish, and a physical reference sample whenever the job must match existing work, so that every later tool and compound choice serves a stated target instead of the polisher's taste.

included: reference sample capture for match jobs
excluded: promising appearance outcomes plating cannot deliver

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a log of finish-dispute rework showing which spec fields were missing when disputes arose would tighten the required spec vocabulary

pros.claim: A written finish spec turns a taste argument into a checkable gate
pros.example: a bracelet specified as directional satin, lengthwise, medium grade, top faces only is accepted or rejected at QC against those words instead of a shrug

cons.claim: Customers often cannot name a finish until they see it, so early specs can be confidently wrong
cons.example: a customer who asked for shiny rejects the mirror result as too new-looking and wanted the soft sheen the piece had when worn

failure_modes: polishing to the brightest achievable surface by default when the customer wanted the original satin character
specifying a finish for the whole piece when only the display faces were quoted
skipping the reference sample on a match job and arguing sheen from memory
acceptance_tests: every job carries a finish class per face, and match jobs carry a physical or photographic reference before work starts
revisit_triggers: the customer changes the desired appearance after seeing a test coupon
QC disputes show the spec vocabulary is too coarse to arbitrate sheen

nodes.definition: Working knowledge of how each triaged substrate class behaves under abrasives, compounds and wheels - consumed as behavior, never as identification, which belongs to triage. Brass cuts predictably and holds edges; copper is soft, smears and loads wheels; zinc die-cast is softer still, blurs detail almost instantly, and its skin often hides subsurface porosity; silver drags and grabs so it scratches even under coloring compound; mild steel cuts slowly and shrugs off pressure that would ruin brass; stainless work-hardens under a dwelling wheel; hollow stamped shells flex and oil-can under wheel pressure; and previously plated surfaces are microns-thin coatings riding on a different metal. Each behavior maps to a plan change: lighter compound, backed hand work, reduced dwell, tumble routing, or a smaller removal budget.

included: cut-rate and smear behavior per substrate class
heat sensitivity and flex of thin constructions
excluded: chemical response of substrates to prep baths

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: shop scrap-and-coupon trials on each substrate class, logged against outcomes, would replace class-level priors with house-verified behavior notes

pros.claim: Behavior knowledge converts one generic buffing routine into per-metal plans that avoid predictable damage
pros.example: routing a zinc die-cast belt buckle to a light greaseless satin pass instead of the tripoli-class buff that would erase its cast detail in seconds

cons.claim: Class-level behavior can mislead on nonstandard alloys and mixed constructions
cons.example: a leaded brass casting smears like copper rather than cutting like sheet brass, loading the wheel the plan said would stay clean

failure_modes: applying brass-speed cutting to die-cast and blurring all cast detail
letting a wheel dwell on stainless until the work-hardened patch polishes differently from its surroundings
treating a previously plated surface as solid metal and cutting through in one pass
acceptance_tests: for each substrate class on the traveler the finishing plan names at least one behavior-driven adjustment or explicitly states none is needed
revisit_triggers: an unfamiliar substrate class or construction starts arriving at the shop
a piece behaves off-class at the wheel (smearing, hardening, flexing) despite a verified traveler

nodes.definition: Set a per-piece metal-removal budget before any abrasive touches it, anchored in how little material the critical layers actually contain. The grounding corpus places flash-class electroplate at hundredths-to-tenths of a micron, the gold-plated marking class near half a micron, heavy-gold-plate and vermeil classes at a few microns, and a gold-filled shell on light-gauge stock in the several-micron class - all cited as handbook or marking-rule classes, not guarantees. Seconds of cut-down buffing can remove more than any of these layers hold, so the budget states what is thinnest and irreplaceable on this piece (old plate to be kept, clad skin, thin walls, crisp detail) and how much leveling those layers can survive; a piece whose defects cannot be fixed inside the budget gets disclosure or referral, not more buffing.

included: identifying the thinnest irreplaceable layer per piece
stating the budget on the traveler before work
class-level thickness reasoning from the corpus
excluded: asserting universal thickness numbers as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cross-section or XRF thickness data on representative incoming work would convert class-level budgets into measured ones and change several refusal thresholds

pros.claim: Budget-first thinking prevents the signature irreversible error of the bench: spending a layer that cannot be repurchased
pros.example: declining to level a deep scratch on a vermeil-class locket because the leveling depth would pass through the entire existing gold class before the scratch bottomed out

cons.claim: Class-level arithmetic is conservative and can refuse work a measured piece would tolerate
cons.example: an unusually heavy old plate would have survived a light cut-down, but the class-based budget said no and the customer went elsewhere

failure_modes: budgeting from the substrate metal while forgetting the coating on top of it is the scarce layer
setting a budget and then not writing it down, so the second session forgets it
quoting corpus thickness classes to the customer as guaranteed measurements of their piece
acceptance_tests: every traveler entering abrasive work states the thinnest irreplaceable layer and the removal budget derived from it
any job whose defect list cannot close inside the budget shows a disclosure or referral note instead of extra passes
revisit_triggers: instrumental thickness measurement becomes available for incoming pieces
a budgeted job still cut through, meaning the class assumptions were too generous

nodes.definition: Inspect the piece under magnification and raking light before finishing and write the defect map: every scratch, pit, dent, corrosion spot, tool mark and worn zone located, with each one classed remove, reduce, or leave-and-disclose. The classing is where honesty meets economics - a fine scratch in reach of the budget is marked remove; a dent is named a dent, because dents are displaced metal that only lifts with repair work, not buffing; a pit field on cast metal is flagged as possible porosity; and anything the budget cannot fix is discussed with the customer now, while expectations are still adjustable. The map, photographed for customer goods, becomes the contract the cut-down stage executes and the QC gate audits.

excluded: post-finishing QC (a later gate reuses the method)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a tally of mid-job discoveries and QC misses attributed to mapping gaps would recalibrate how deep the standard map must go per job class

pros.claim: Classing defects before work converts mid-job surprises into up-front conversations
pros.example: showing the customer at intake that the case-back sports a dent that polishing cannot lift, instead of explaining it after hours of buffing failed to

cons.claim: A thorough map costs bench time on cheap jobs where the finisher would find the same defects en route
cons.example: fifteen minutes of mapping on a batch of plain brass key fobs whose every defect the first tripoli-class pass would have handled anyway

failure_modes: classifying a dent as a scratch and chasing displaced metal deeper into the budget
mapping under overhead light only and missing the fine scratch field raking light would have shown
skipping the photo record and losing a was-it-there-before dispute
acceptance_tests: every defect on the map carries a class and every disclose item has customer acknowledgment before work begins
revisit_triggers: QC failures reveal defect types the mapping vocabulary does not capture
mid-job discoveries exceed a tolerable rate, meaning mapping is too shallow

nodes.definition: Take deep, localized defects down with graded hand abrasives - papers, sticks and rubberized blocks worked in sequence - before any wheel touches the piece. The governing mechanism: each abrasive grade exists solely to remove the scratches of the grade before it, so a skipped grade leaves scratches no later stage can honestly hide, and they telegraph through color buffing and through the thin plate itself. Hand work also does what a wheel cannot: it keeps flats flat and edges square by working against a backing, where a mop wraps around geometry and rounds everything it meets. The sequence starts at the finest grade that actually reaches the defect - starting coarse to save minutes spends the removal budget wholesale.

included: grade-by-grade sequencing per the abrasive maker's grading
backed work on flats and edges
excluded: texture creation (a dedicated unit owns satin and matte)
dent raising and other repair work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: coupon tests logging which grade sequences close which defect depths on each substrate would replace rule-of-thumb grade choices

pros.claim: Backed hand abrasives remove a deep scratch while preserving the surrounding geometry a wheel would wash out
pros.example: sanding a gouge out of a flat cigarette-case lid over a hardwood block leaves the lid flat, where the buff would have dished a bright hollow around the gouge

cons.claim: Hand sequencing is slow and its cost scales with every grade the defect demands
cons.example: one deep scratch on a watch case-back pulls four successive grades and half an hour before the piece may even meet the cutting buff

failure_modes: skipping a grade to save time and finding the coarse scratches again under the color buff
sanding unbacked with finger pressure and rippling a flat surface
starting at the coarsest grade by habit and tripling the metal removed
acceptance_tests: before wheel work, each hand-worked zone shows only the final grade's uniform scratch pattern under raking light
revisit_triggers: telegraphed scratches appear at QC in zones logged as hand-finished

nodes.definition: The cut-down stage: firmer buffs - spiral-sewn cotton and treated wheels - charged with a cutting-class compound remove the hand-abrasive pattern and level the broad surface toward the target. This is where nearly all wheel-driven metal loss occurs, so it runs inside the stated budget with deliberate technique: moderate pressure so the compound cuts instead of burnishing smeared metal over debris, passes crossed against the previous direction so leveling can be seen honestly, the work kept moving so no zone dwells hot, and the piece held below the wheel centerline so a snatch throws it away from the operator. Cut-down ends when the surface carries only the uniform fine pattern the coloring stage can close - continuing past that point is pure budget burn.

included: wheel and pressure technique for cutting
excluded: any work over flagged marks or joints without the mark unit's clearance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: before-and-after weight or profilometer readings on coupons per wheel-compound pairing would quantify the stage's real removal rates and tighten budget math

pros.claim: A competent cut-down produces the leveled canvas that makes both mirror and satin targets achievable in one further stage
pros.example: a scratched brass locket emerging from cut-down with one uniform fine pattern that a single color pass turns into a flawless mirror

cons.claim: The cutting stage is the most destructive tool on the bench and amplifies every planning error
cons.example: an extra thirty seconds of tripoli-class work on a plated tray erases the old plate entirely and turns a brighten-it job into a strip-and-replate negotiation

failure_modes: pressing harder as the compound wears out and burnishing debris into the surface instead of cutting
dwelling on one spot to kill a stubborn scratch and dishing a visible hollow
cutting past done because a brighter surface felt like progress, spending budget the color stage did not need
acceptance_tests: after cut-down the surface shows a single uniform fine scratch pattern under raking light, with no dishing at defect sites and all flagged zones untouched
removal stayed inside the traveler's stated budget for every zone
revisit_triggers: QC repeatedly finds dishing or residual coarse scratches after cut-down
the compound maker's product or grading for the cutting class changes

nodes.definition: The coloring stage: soft loose-sewn muslin or flannel mops charged with a coloring-class compound raise the leveled cut-down surface to final luster with near-negligible removal. Color work is a closer, not a fixer - it makes whatever pattern exists brighter, so a scratch entering the color stage exits as a brilliantly polished scratch; the only correct response to a defect discovered here is to go back a stage, never to press harder. Technique is light: low pressure, fresh compound in small amounts, the work floated against the mop and kept moving, because a dwelling color mop generates heat fast on thin sections and drags soft metals like silver into fresh micro-scratching.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a defect-tagged QC log distinguishing color-stage scratching from contamination and cut-down carryover would isolate how often this stage is the true culprit

pros.claim: Coloring delivers the mirror the customer actually sees while consuming almost none of the removal budget
pros.example: a properly cut-down pendant reaching a swipe-clean mirror in two minutes of rouge-class work with no measurable dimensional change

cons.claim: Because color work flatters everything, it hides process failures until the QC light finds them
cons.example: a glittering bracelet that looks finished on the bench but shows an army of fine parallel scratches the moment raking light crosses it

failure_modes: trying to color out a cut-down scratch by pressure and heat instead of stepping back a stage
over-charging the mop so compound cakes into recesses the degrease line must then fight
buffing a hollow piece to temperature until a solder seam lets go
acceptance_tests: the colored surface passes raking-light inspection with no residual pattern coarser than the finish class allows
revisit_triggers: recurring fine-scratch findings at QC point at the color mop or its compound

nodes.definition: Choose the compound family for each stage-substrate pairing per the compound maker's guidance: cutting classes (tripoli and emery-bar types) for cut-down on copper alloys and steel, milder cutting or direct-to-color routes for soft zinc die-cast and silver, dedicated coloring classes (rouge types and modern white-finish bars) per metal for luster, and greaseless satin compounds where a brushed sheen is the target. Selection also owns a forward-looking duty the tank enforces later: compound residue is the single most common cleaning failure upstream of plating, so the choice weighs how the binder behaves - how it loads into recesses, whether it dries hard with age, and what the shop's degrease line has proven it can remove - because a compound the cleaning line cannot strip is the wrong compound no matter how well it cuts.

included: stage-substrate compound matching per maker guidance
binder cleanability as a selection criterion
compound change notes on the traveler
excluded: improvising or blending compounds outside maker guidance
wheel lifecycle management (the dedication unit owns it)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: degrease-line water-break statistics broken out by compound family would turn cleanability from folklore into a ranked selection table

pros.claim: Choosing compounds with the cleaning line in mind prevents the classic prep failure of plating over invisible grease
pros.example: swapping a heavy-binder cutting bar for the maker's easier-cleaning equivalent after the degrease line kept finding water-break failures in stamped recesses

cons.claim: The cleanability-first choice can cost cutting speed on hard jobs
cons.example: the easier-cleaning bar needs two extra passes on a mild-steel buckle that the aggressive bar leveled in one

failure_modes: using one favorite bar for everything and discovering it neither cuts steel nor colors silver properly
picking an aggressive compound whose baked binder survives the shop's degreaser
leaving the compound family off the traveler so the chemical line cannot anticipate its residue
acceptance_tests: every stage on the finishing plan names its compound family and the traveler records what was actually used
revisit_triggers: the degrease line reports rising water-break failures traced to compound residue
a compound maker discontinues or reformulates a family in use

nodes.definition: Enforce the shop law that defeats cross-contamination: every wheel and mop carries exactly one compound for its entire life, is labeled with it, is raked regularly to expose fresh face, and is stored so compounds never touch. The mechanism is unforgiving - a single crumb of cutting grit embedded in a coloring mop re-scratches every subsequent piece at the very stage meant to remove scratches, and the failure is invisible until raking light finds the recurring fine parallel lines. Dedication extends to hazard carryover: a wheel that has touched a lead-solder repair or suspect leaded alloy is contaminated in a different sense, smearing lead onto later work where it poisons plating adhesion, so suspect wheels are quarantined or retired rather than cleaned by hope.

excluded: tumbling media hygiene (the media unit owns its own)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a scratch-recurrence log before and after dedication tightening would quantify how much QC failure the rule actually absorbs in this shop

pros.claim: Strict dedication makes contamination a bounded event instead of a shop-wide epidemic
pros.example: when a color mop starts scratching, the label system condemns one wheel instead of forcing suspicion over every mop on the rack

cons.claim: Dedication multiplies wheel inventory and storage cost for small shops
cons.example: three compounds across cutting, coloring and satin work on two spindle tapers already demand six labeled wheels where a careless shop keeps two

failure_modes: borrowing the color mop for one quick tripoli-class touch-up and scrapping its coloring career invisibly
storing bare wheels in one drawer where compound dust migrates between them
keeping a lead-suspect wheel in service because it still cuts well
acceptance_tests: every wheel in the shop carries a legible compound label and no unlabeled wheel is mounted
a suspect-contamination report quarantines the wheel the same day, with pieces since the last clean QC re-inspected
revisit_triggers: recurring fine scratches at QC with no change in compounds or technique
a lead-solder or leaded-alloy piece is discovered to have been buffed on a general-service wheel

nodes.definition: Protect what the wheel destroys fastest: crisp edges, milgrain, engraving, chased and cast detail, and above all hallmarks and maker's marks. A mop wraps around geometry, so high, sharp features take the full cut while flats barely feel it - detail visibly softens in seconds and the loss is absolute, since no bench operation restores a struck mark or a chased line. Hallmarks carry a second weight: they are the piece's marking evidence under jurisdiction-dependent marking regimes, and the corpus's marking-rule classes make clear that identity claims trace to such marks - so a hallmark is never polished out, and any deliberate work over marks or detail requires the documented customer sign-off from triage, executed with masking tape dams, thumb shielding, felt sticks and hand work in place of the wheel near protected features.

included: mark and detail inventory before work
sign-off verification before any work over marks

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: jurisdictional guidance or a trade-body ruling on altered hallmarks would harden this from shop discipline into an explicit compliance procedure

pros.claim: A mark-and-detail inventory taped to the bench keeps the wheel away from the ten seconds that would ruin the job
pros.example: masking the hallmark panel of a silver-gilt spoon before cut-down so the struck lion and date letter survive a full refinish untouched

cons.claim: Aggressive protection leaves visible finish transitions around protected zones
cons.example: the masked square around a case-back hallmark reads as a dull window in an otherwise mirror surface and needs careful hand blending at its border

failure_modes: one absent-minded pass over an unmasked hallmark reducing it to an unreadable smudge
polishing a crisp engraved monogram into a soft ghost because the mop wrapped the corner
accepting a verbal it-is-fine for mark removal instead of the documented sign-off
acceptance_tests: before wheel work every mark and protected detail is inventoried and physically masked or route-planned around
after finishing, every hallmark is legible at the same magnification as at intake, or a countersigned sign-off covers the change
revisit_triggers: any post-job discovery that a mark or detail changed without paperwork
the shop starts taking a class of goods with unfamiliar marking conventions

nodes.definition: The stop discipline that defines professional restraint on customer goods: remove only what the agreed defect map authorizes, stop when the target finish spec is met, and treat every pass beyond that as unpaid risk taken on someone else's property. The pull to keep going is real - the piece visibly improves under the wheel, and could-look-better is always true - but each extra pass spends wall thickness, plate, detail crispness and budget that the customer never agreed to trade. The rule binds hardest mid-job: when something unexpected surfaces, the answer is stop, photograph, re-contact, because continuing under uncertainty converts a recoverable situation into an apology. On shop-owned production stock the calculus may relax; on customer goods it never does.

excluded: negotiating new work scope with the customer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: dispute and rework records tying outcomes to stop-discipline adherence would show whether the line is drawn at the right strictness

pros.claim: Stopping at spec caps the shop's liability at what was quoted and agreed
pros.example: leaving the faint disclosed scratch on a locket lid exactly as disclosed, so the delivered piece matches the conversation instead of surprising the owner with a thinner lid

cons.claim: Disciplined stopping can read as underdelivery next to a competitor who buffs everything bright
cons.example: a customer comparing the honest satin-with-one-scratch result against another shop's glossy over-buffed job and preferring the shinier lie

failure_modes: chasing the last five percent of a defect through the piece's remaining budget
improving unrequested surfaces while the piece is on the wheel anyway
continuing after an unexpected breakthrough because stopping felt like failure
acceptance_tests: delivered work matches the defect map's remove list and nothing beyond it, verified against intake photographs
every mid-job surprise in the log shows a stop-and-recontact entry before further work
revisit_triggers: a pattern of customer complaints that disclosed defects were expected to be gone
budget overruns recur despite stops, meaning the spec-met endpoint is being misjudged

nodes.definition: Know when a pit is a pit and when it is the mouth of a sponge. On wrought sheet a surface pit usually bottoms out and can be leveled inside budget; on castings and above all on zinc die-cast, pits frequently connect to subsurface porosity, and cutting deeper opens more voids than it removes - the surface degrades as work proceeds, which is itself the diagnostic. Opened porosity is a plating disaster in waiting: pores trap compound and later process solutions, then bleed out through the deposit as stains and blisters. The discipline: probe the first pit conservatively, stop at the first sign that pits multiply or enlarge under cutting, and route the decision - fill-and-repair referral, seal-class options discussed downstream, or leave-and-disclose - back through the customer rather than deeper into the metal.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: sectioning a few condemned die-cast zones to see actual void structure versus bench judgment would calibrate the stop-on-multiplication threshold

pros.claim: Early porosity recognition saves the whole downstream chain from plating a doomed surface
pros.example: stopping after the second probe pass on a die-cast buckle whose one pit became five, and quoting repair-or-disclose instead of a plate job that would blister

cons.claim: Conservative probing sometimes abandons defects that one more honest pass would have cleared
cons.example: a shallow pit field on a brass casting written up for disclosure although it would have leveled out just past the probe depth

failure_modes: chasing a die-cast pit until the panel is visibly dished and still porous
reading multiplying pits as insufficient effort rather than as the porosity signature
leveling a porous zone smooth enough to look sound and passing it silently to the tank
acceptance_tests: any zone where pits multiplied or enlarged under cutting is flagged on the traveler with the stop depth and the customer-facing recommendation
revisit_triggers: the plating line reports blistering or bleed-out traced to a zone this unit passed as sound

nodes.definition: Manage the special case of finishing a piece that is already plated: the existing deposit is a coating measured in the corpus's sub-micron to few-micron classes, so cut-down speed that is safe on solid brass erases it in moments, and a breakthrough exposes a patch of different metal that colors differently now and behaves differently in every downstream step. The unit's decisions: whether the old plate is to be kept (light color work only, no cutting), feathered (blending a worn edge without enlarging it), or deliberately cut through as a step toward strip-and-replate - the last being irreversible and thus requiring the documented sign-off, with the stripping itself belonging to chemistry, not the wheel. An accidental breakthrough mid-job is a stop-photograph-recontact event, never something to quietly buff wider in the hope of evening it out.

included: keep vs feather vs cut-through decision
excluded: adhesion diagnosis of the old plate (triage flags it)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured thickness of old plate on a sample of incoming replate work would replace class assumptions in the keep/feather/cut decision

pros.claim: Deciding keep-feather-or-cut before wheel time replaces the worst mid-job surprise with a planned route
pros.example: classifying a worn teapot as feather-only at the spout wear zones and keep elsewhere, so no one discovers pink copper mid-buff

cons.claim: Feathering worn plate is skilled slow work that can exceed the cost of stripping on badly worn goods
cons.example: an hour of edge-blending on a tray whose plate was so far gone that a strip authorization would have served the customer better

failure_modes: treating a plated surface as solid metal and cutting through on the first pass
buffing a small accidental breakthrough wider to blend it and tripling the exposed patch
starting a deliberate cut-through on verbal approval with the sign-off still unsigned
acceptance_tests: every previously plated job carries a keep/feather/cut-through class per zone before wheel work
no deliberate cut-through begins without the countersigned authorization on file
revisit_triggers: accidental breakthroughs recur on jobs classed keep, meaning the class-level thickness assumptions are too generous
the shop adds thickness instrumentation that can measure old plate before classing

nodes.definition: Manage wheel work around joints and repairs, where friction heat and mechanical drag do damage the rest of the piece never sees. Low-melt lead-tin repair solder - common on old costume goods and amateur repairs - smears under a warm buff, dragging a grey film across the surrounding surface that reads as discoloration and behaves as a plating poison the activation line cannot fully rescue; the same wheel is now lead-contaminated for future work. Legitimate jewelry solder joints tolerate buffing but sit proud or hollow, so the mop preferentially cuts them and a dwelling pass trench-lines a seam. Thin sections and hollow constructions heat in seconds, discoloring, warping, or letting a low-temperature seam creep. Technique: hand-finish over and around flagged joints, keep wheel passes moving parallel to seams rather than across them, and treat any grey streak appearing near a joint as an immediate stop-and-flag event.

included: joint-zone route planning from traveler flags
heat and dwell discipline near seams and thin sections
excluded: chemical response of solders in prep baths

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: spot-test screening of repair joints at triage, logged against smear events at the bench, would sharpen which flags genuinely demand hand-only work

pros.claim: Hand-finishing flagged joint zones contains the one contamination that spreads from piece to wheel to shop
pros.example: working a felt stick over a suspected lead repair on a vintage brooch while the wheel handles the rest, so no grey film and no condemned mop

cons.claim: Joint caution slows every vintage and repaired piece even when the flag proves unfounded
cons.example: hand-finishing around a seam the traveler flagged as suspect that turns out to be sound silver solder all along

failure_modes: buffing across an unnoticed lead repair and dragging grey smear over the display face
dwelling on a proud seam until a trench outlines the joint
returning a wheel that touched suspect solder to general service
acceptance_tests: every flagged joint zone on the traveler shows its planned finishing method before wheel work, and no grey-streak event proceeds without a stop-and-flag entry
revisit_triggers: the chemical line or plating line reports joint-adjacent defects on pieces this unit passed
a wheel-contamination event traces back to an unflagged repair

nodes.definition: Route each job between the polishing wheel and mass finishing before any work starts, because the two paths do not meet in the middle: the wheel gives per-piece control, local correction and true mirror capability at the price of per-piece labor and catch risk; tumbling gives batch economy, uniform all-over treatment and access to recesses at the price of edge softening, no local control, and a sheen ceiling below true color-buffed mirror. One rule in this unit is absolute and safety-anchored: chains, flexible link goods and anything that can wrap never meet a spinning buff - a caught chain whips the piece and the hand holding it into the wheel - so such goods go to tumble-burnishing or hand methods unconditionally. Beyond that, the decision weighs piece value, count, geometry, target finish and removal budget: high-count uniform small parts tumble; one customer heirloom with a defect map gets the wheel and hands.

included: route decision per job before work
excluded: media and cycle specifics (the media unit)
safety rule ownership (the safety unit sets station rules; this unit obeys them)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: route-versus-outcome records (rework rate, cycle cost, sheen acceptance) per job class would refine the routing thresholds beyond rules of thumb

pros.claim: Routing before work prevents the expensive hybrid where half-wheeled pieces then tumble to a different sheen
pros.example: committing a fifty-piece pendant batch to tumble-then-spot-check instead of wheel-finishing twelve of them first and discovering the sheens never match

cons.claim: Hard routing rules occasionally force the slow path on goods that a skilled hand could have wheeled safely
cons.example: a stout curb chain a veteran might brighten by hand-held technique still goes to the tumbler, costing a day of cycle time

failure_modes: bringing a necklace to the buff because it is quick and finding out why the rule exists
tumbling a mirror-spec job and hoping burnishing will pass for color work
splitting a batch across routes and delivering two visibly different finishes
acceptance_tests: every traveler shows a wheel/tumble/hand route decision recorded before finishing begins, and no linked or flexible item is ever routed to the wheel
revisit_triggers: batch sheen complaints reveal the routing rule of thumb misjudged a finish class
new media or equipment changes what the tumble route can achieve

nodes.definition: Operate mass finishing by mechanism, not recipe: hardened steel shot with burnishing soap glosses by plastic deformation - it moves metal and removes essentially none, which is why the corpus names burnishing the correct finish class for microns-thin gold skins and why it is the default for anything whose surface layer is the product; abrasive ceramic and plastic media genuinely remove metal, useful for deburring and pre-finish smoothing on solid stock but forbidden on thin-skinned goods; magnetic pin finishers reach interior recesses no other method touches, with the corpus-flagged caveat that overuse peens a visible texture onto the work. Cycle times and soap dosing follow the media and compound maker's label; media hygiene mirrors wheel dedication - contaminated or degraded media scratches instead of finishing, and shot must be kept soaped and dry between runs or it corrodes and prints rust into every subsequent load.

included: burnishing vs abrasive media mechanism choice
media hygiene and shot care per maker label
excluded: waste-water handling from tumblers (chemical-line and jurisdiction rules govern)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logged batch outcomes per media-compound-cycle combination would build the house table that replaces label-plus-guess cycle planning

pros.claim: Steel-shot burnishing finishes goods no wheel can safely touch while spending none of the removal budget
pros.example: a tangle-prone batch of chain bracelets emerging uniformly glossed from a shot-and-soap cycle with their thin old plate intact

cons.claim: Mass finishing is statistical, so a bad cycle degrades the whole batch before anyone sees a piece
cons.example: one load run with tired abrasive media dulling forty pendants that then all need individual recovery on the wheel

failure_modes: running abrasive media on thin-plated goods because the hopper was already loaded
leaving steel shot wet over a weekend and rust-printing the next three loads
extending a magnetic-pin cycle to chase gloss and peening matte texture into detail
acceptance_tests: each cycle's traveler names media class, compound and cycle intent, and thin-skinned goods never see abrasive media
a sampled piece from every batch passes raking-light inspection before the batch moves on
revisit_triggers: batch defects trace to media condition or the wrong media class
a media or compound maker revises its product line or label guidance

nodes.definition: Produce non-mirror targets deliberately: directional satin from greaseless-compound wheels, abrasive brushes or hand rubbing with graded pads, always laid in one stated direction; non-directional matte from bead-blast-class treatment or fine media tumbling; scratch-brushed sheens from wire wheels run per their maker's intent. Texture is applied over an already-leveled surface as the last mechanical step, because texture hides nothing - a scratch under satin telegraphs exactly as it does under mirror - and because any later buffing pass flattens the texture's peaks into shiny streaks that force complete re-texturing. Matching an existing texture on partial refinish work is its own skill: direction, grade and coverage are matched on a test coupon against the reference sample before touching the piece, since a close-but-wrong satin reads worse on a mixed panel than an honest full refinish would.

included: directional satin, matte and scratch-brush production
excluded: chemical or electrochemical matting of any kind

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a retained coupon library with acceptance outcomes would standardize the shop's satin grades into a named, repeatable set

pros.claim: Coupon-first matching turns sheen matching from gamble into comparison
pros.example: three quick satin coupons at different grades held against the customer's watch bracelet picking the right one before the piece is ever touched

cons.claim: Texture work is fragile right up to handoff because one careless touch undoes it
cons.example: a finished lengthwise-satin lighter picking up a glossy streak from a single accidental swipe against the color mop en route to QC

failure_modes: texturing over an unleveled surface and watching the scratches telegraph through the satin
laying satin in the wrong direction and having the panel flash differently from its neighbors
color-buffing after texturing out of habit and flattening the finish into streaks
acceptance_tests: textured surfaces match the reference coupon for direction, grade and coverage under raking light, and the coupon is retained with the job record
revisit_triggers: sheen-match complaints on delivered partial refinishes
a new texture class enters the shop's offering

nodes.definition: Apply the hardest limits on the bench to goods whose surface is the product: gold-filled and rolled-gold-plate items carry a wrought karat skin fixed at the mill in the several-micron class - the corpus is blunt that every micron removed is the product and that burnishing, not abrasion, is the correct finishing class, since the construction cannot be restored by any bench operation and re-plating over damage destroys the marking class the customer paid for. Worn-through or scratched clad goods get burnish-and-disclose, with any abrasive work requiring the documented sign-off. Antique gilt goods carry a second, harsher rule: suspected fire-gilt (ormolu) work can retain residual mercury from the amalgam process, and the corpus records mechanically refinishing or heating such objects as a recognized conservation-class hazard - so suspected fire-gilt work is refused at the bench and referred to conservation, without exception and without a sign-off path, because no customer signature makes mercury exposure acceptable.

included: sign-off requirement for any abrasive work on clad goods
unconditional refusal of suspected fire-gilt refinishing
excluded: identifying GF/RGP construction (triage, with its cert and test caveats)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a documented shop protocol for mercury-suspect intake (screening, refusal wording, referral partners) validated against conservation guidance would firm up this unit's referral half

pros.claim: Burnish-only handling lets the shop service clad heirlooms without spending the customer's irreplaceable gold
pros.example: reviving a dulled gold-filled pocket-watch chain by steel-shot burnishing and returning it with its full skin and its GF character intact

cons.claim: Refusal rules turn away real revenue and can send customers to shops that will do the harm
cons.example: declining to polish a fire-gilt candelabrum and watching the customer take it to someone with a buffing wheel and no idea

failure_modes: one cut-down session converting a gold-filled bangle into a brass bangle with gold traces
buffing suspected ormolu and aerosolizing mercury-bearing dust at an unextracted station
accepting a sign-off as license to abrade a clad skin the customer did not understand was finite
acceptance_tests: no abrasive process touches a GF/RGP-flagged piece without the countersigned authorization, and burnish-only jobs show zero abrasive steps on the traveler
every suspected fire-gilt piece in the log shows refusal and referral, never bench work
revisit_triggers: triage revises how clad construction or fire-gilt suspicion is flagged
a conservation or jurisdictional guidance update changes handling duties for mercury-suspect objects

nodes.definition: Run the polishing station under explicit obligation classes, verified against the jurisdiction's workplace rules rather than assumed: machine guarding on wheel nips; eye protection always; dust control as extraction at the wheel hood plus respiratory protection classes for fine polishing dust, which carries compound binder and whatever metal the shop cuts - a serious matter when that includes lead-solder work or leaded alloys; work-holding rules - no chains or flexible goods at the wheel, no loose clothing, hair tied, no wound-on gloves that can drag a hand in, the piece gripped below the wheel centerline so a snatch throws it clear; and training before solo wheel time. Dust and sweeps are materials, not dirt: polishing waste from gilded or previously plated goods is metal-bearing and routes to a refiner, lead-suspect dust is segregated hazardous material, and local disposal rules are treated as unknown until verified. Safety obligations outrank every schedule pressure on the bench, in line with the program-wide rule that safety and compliance beat throughput, cost and deadline.

included: guarding, PPE and extraction obligation classes
work-holding and clothing rules at the wheel
excluded: chemical-line safety (cyanide/acid segregation lives with chemistry and is absolute there)
medical advice on exposure - route to professional care

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a completed jurisdiction-verification file (workplace dust rules, waste routing, training duties) would convert several obligation classes here into named local requirements

pros.claim: Stated obligation classes make safety auditable instead of tribal
pros.example: a new hire's checklist covering guard position, extraction on, glasses on, hair tied, grip zone - checkable by anyone in thirty seconds

cons.claim: Class-level rules still need local completion, which takes real effort
cons.example: the shop must still find and apply its own jurisdiction's dust-exposure and waste rules, since this KB deliberately asserts no limit values

failure_modes: running the wheel with extraction off for one quick pass and breathing the session's finest dust
sweeping lead-suspect polishing dust into general trash
letting an untrained hand buff because the backlog was deep
acceptance_tests: the station passes its obligation-class checklist (guarding, extraction, PPE, work-holding, training) before any session, and violations stop work regardless of deadline
metal-bearing and lead-suspect dust streams are segregated and their routing is documented
revisit_triggers: any near-miss or incident at the station
a change in jurisdictional workplace or waste rules, or in what metal classes the shop cuts

nodes.definition: Audit the finished surface against the target finish spec before the piece may leave mechanical finishing: raking light and magnification over every face; no scratch pattern coarser than the finish class permits and no telegraphed defects from skipped stages; texture direction, grade and coverage matching the reference coupon on non-mirror work; detail crisp and every hallmark legible as at intake unless covered by sign-off; dimensions and fit unchanged where the job specifies them; and, on customer goods, the after photographs that close the loop the intake photographs opened. The gate exists because the tank is a magnifier with no undo - a flaw that passes here returns gold-plated - and its second product is information: every failure is tagged to its causing stage so the shop learns where its process leaks.

excluded: cleanliness verification (the water-break test belongs to chemistry)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: correlating gate records with downstream plating defects would show which checks predict tank outcomes and which are ritual

pros.claim: A hard gate before chemistry is the last cheap moment to catch a finish flaw
pros.example: raking light catching the faint parallel scratch field from a contaminated mop while it is a re-buff, not a strip-and-redo after plating

cons.claim: Gate rigor adds latency and can bottleneck a one-person shop
cons.example: a full-face raking-light audit with photographs adding meaningful minutes to every piece on a fifty-piece day

failure_modes: inspecting under bench overhead light and passing what raking light would fail
gating only the display face while the reverse carries cut-down scratches
passing a borderline surface because the schedule needed it gone
acceptance_tests: every released piece has a recorded gate result covering spec match, detail and hallmark state, and photos for customer goods
every gate failure carries a stage tag feeding the shop's defect statistics
revisit_triggers: downstream (chemistry or plating) reports surface defects on gated pieces
gate failure statistics shift, indicating an upstream stage drifted

nodes.definition: Close mechanical finishing by handing the chemical prep line a piece it can actually clean, with a traveler that tells it what it is cleaning: the compound family used at each stage (grease-class or greaseless, so the line can anticipate the residue), zones flagged for special attention (suspect solder smear, opened pores that will trap solution, masked areas where tape adhesive remains), the route taken (wheel, tumble, hand) and the finish class delivered. Timing is the quiet rule of this unit: fresh compound residue is the degrease line's normal input, but residue that sits for days hardens in recesses and ages toward uncleanable, so finished work routes to degrease promptly rather than accumulating on a shelf. What this unit never does is chemistry - no wipe-downs with improvised solvents, no quick dips; the boundary to the chemical line is a handoff of information and a physical piece, nothing else.

included: traveler completion (compound family, flags, route, finish class)
physical transfer without surface contact on finished faces
excluded: any cleaning step including solvent wipes
the water-break test and rinse discipline (chemistry)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: chem-line cleaning outcomes correlated with traveler completeness and handoff delay would prove which fields and time limits actually matter

pros.claim: A residue-aware traveler lets the degrease line choose its process instead of discovering the compound the hard way
pros.example: the chem line pre-treating a heavy grease-bar job differently from a greaseless-satin job because the traveler said which was coming

cons.claim: Prompt-routing discipline fights natural batching economics
cons.example: walking single finished pieces to degrease through the day instead of accumulating a tidy end-of-day tray that would sit overnight

failure_modes: finished pieces aging on the bench until compound hardens in every recess
a traveler that omits the solder-smear flag, so the line activates a zone that can never come clean
an improvised solvent wipe at the bench that smears residue into a film the degreaser struggles with
acceptance_tests: every handoff includes the completed traveler fields and a routing timestamp showing prompt transfer to the chemical line
revisit_triggers: degrease-line feedback on hardened residue or missing flags
the chemical line changes its degrease chemistry and needs different information

edges.why_related: a finish target can only be set for a piece whose identity, coatings and permissions are verified in the triage packet
behavior knowledge is indexed by the substrate class the triage packet certifies; without the verdict there is nothing to look up
the removal budget is built on how the certified substrate and its coatings behave and how much material their thin layers hold
defect mapping starts from the triage packet's flags (repairs, coatings, porosity suspicion) and adds the surface survey on top
defect classing depends on the target: a scratch acceptable under matte may be a must-remove under mirror
hand-abrasive work executes exactly the deep-defect removals the map authorizes and nothing else
cut-down levels toward the map's agreed outcome; without the map it is uncontrolled metal removal
the cutting stage runs on the compound family selection assigned to it for this substrate and stage
the budget is the binding limit inside which all cut-down work must stay
color work can only close the uniform fine pattern a completed cut-down leaves; it cannot fix what cut-down missed
compound families are matched to the substrate's cut, smear and drag behavior per the maker's guidance
the dedication regime exists per compound family in use; each selected family demands its own labeled wheels
the route decision hinges on whether the specified finish class is reachable by the tumble path at all
media mechanics are exercised only for jobs the routing decision sent to mass finishing
texture work exists to produce the direction, grade and coverage the finish spec names
the thin-skin rules are the budget logic taken to its extreme: on clad goods the budget for abrasion is effectively zero
the stop discipline enforces exactly the remove list the map agreed; the map defines what stopping honestly means
the budget supplies the quantitative line the stop discipline holds
keep, feather or cut-through is budget arithmetic on the corpus's coating thickness classes
the gate audits the colored surface as the finished product of the mirror route
the gate audits textured surfaces against the retained reference coupon
only gated pieces hand off; the gate record is part of what the traveler carries forward
guarding, extraction, PPE and work-holding obligations bound every cutting session before productivity is even discussed
edges.risk_of_conflict: schedule pressure tempting an unextracted or unguarded quick pass

edges.why_related: the no-chains-at-the-wheel rule is a safety obligation the routing decision must obey unconditionally
edges.risk_of_conflict: a confident operator arguing a specific chain is safe to hand-hold at the buff

edges.why_related: cut-down routes around masked marks and protected detail; no pass crosses them without the sign-off
edges.risk_of_conflict: a leveling pass that would be easier taken straight across a hallmark panel

edges.why_related: the finest-grade-that-reaches-it start rule is the stop discipline expressed at the sanding bench
edges.risk_of_conflict: starting coarse to save time on a defect the budget barely covers

edges.why_related: clad and thin-plated goods are restricted to burnishing media; abrasive media on them is forbidden regardless of batch convenience
edges.risk_of_conflict: a mixed batch where re-loading the tumbler for one clad piece feels wasteful

edges.why_related: the cutting stage wants the defect gone; the stop discipline wants the metal kept - the same pass serves one against the other
edges.resolution_rule: on customer goods the stop discipline wins: when the budget or the agreed remove list is reached, cutting ends and the remainder is disclosed, never chased

edges.why_related: batch economics push work toward the tumbler while the spec may name a sheen the tumble route cannot reach
edges.resolution_rule: the agreed finish spec wins: a batch routes to mass finishing only when the media route demonstrably reaches the specified class, else wheel time is scheduled

edges.why_related: cut-down wants to level the pitted zone; porosity limits say deeper cutting opens more voids than it removes
edges.resolution_rule: at the first sign pits multiply or enlarge under cutting, the porosity rule wins: stop at the recorded depth and route to referral or disclosure

edges.why_related: leveling wants uniform cutting force; a keep-classed old plate cannot survive cutting at all
edges.resolution_rule: the keep/feather/cut-through class wins: keep zones receive color-only work, feather zones blending only, and cutting through requires the countersigned authorization before the first pass

edges.why_related: a uniform mirror spec collides with detail preservation wherever protected features interrupt the surface
edges.resolution_rule: preservation wins by default: the spec is amended to bright-with-preserved-detail and the customer informed; only the documented sign-off can trade detail for uniformity

edges.why_related: a breached dedication regime causes the signature QC finding: recurring fine parallel scratches at the coloring stage
a missed lead smear at the bench becomes a zone the chemical line cannot activate and the tank cannot cover - the flag on the traveler is the containment
skipped grades at the sanding bench cause the telegraphed scratches that surface at the coloring stage two steps later
texture is laid over a leveled cut-down surface as the last mechanical step; texturing before leveling is wasted work
tumbled batches move to piece-sampled gate inspection after the cycle, before any batch is released onward
gate failures tagged by stage flow back into how deep and how skeptical the next defect maps must be
degrease-line reports of stubborn residue re-rank the compound families selection is allowed to use

conflict_axes.name: defect_thoroughness_vs_metal_budget
conflict_axes.description: Every defect looks removable with one more pass, but the pass spends wall thickness, coating and detail the customer never agreed to trade; the tension between a flawless surface and minimum removal runs through every cutting decision.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the written budget and the defect map's remove list are the contract; what they cannot fix is disclosed, and on customer goods disclosure always beats one more pass

conflict_axes.name: mirror_uniformity_vs_detail_preservation
conflict_axes.description: A full mirror wants every square millimeter cut and colored, but detail, milgrain, engraving and hallmarks die under exactly that treatment; the brightest possible piece and the most intact piece are different pieces.
poles: crisp detail and legible marks intact
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: preservation dominates without paperwork: mask and hand-work protected features, amend the spec to bright-with-detail, and only a documented sign-off unlocks trading features for finish

conflict_axes.name: batch_economy_vs_piece_control
conflict_axes.description: Mass finishing amortizes labor across a load but surrenders per-piece judgment; the wheel gives control and mirror capability but costs skilled minutes per piece and adds catch risk on awkward geometry.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route by what the finish spec and the piece's value demand, not by what the schedule prefers; customer heirlooms default to the controlled path, uniform production lots to the batch path

conflict_axes.name: cutting_speed_vs_heat_and_joint_damage
conflict_axes.description: Aggressive compound, pressure and dwell clear defects fastest, but the same energy heats thin sections, trenches solder seams and smears low-melt repairs into plating poison.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: flagged joints and thin constructions cap aggression regardless of schedule: moving passes, moderate pressure, hand work over suspect zones

conflict_axes.name: surface_perfection_vs_porosity_opening
conflict_axes.description: Leveling a pitted zone promises a perfect surface, but on cast and die-cast goods the cutting that chases pits opens the porosity beneath them, trading a visible flaw for an invisible plating failure.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: probe conservatively and let the metal vote: multiplying or enlarging pits end the cutting and route the zone to referral or disclosure

conflict_axes.name: keep_old_plate_vs_uniform_new_substrate
conflict_axes.description: Preserving serviceable old plate saves the customer money and history but constrains finishing to gentle work; cutting through toward strip-and-replate gives a uniform canvas but is irreversible and needs authorization and chemistry.
poles: preserve and feather the existing plate
cut through and hand to strip-and-replate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: class every zone keep, feather or cut-through before wheel time; the cut-through class exists only with the countersigned sign-off, and stripping itself is the chemical line's work

conflict_axes.name: compound_versatility_vs_contamination_control
conflict_axes.description: A few do-everything wheels and bars minimize inventory and changeovers, while strict per-compound dedication multiplies wheels but is the only reliable defense against grit carryover and lead spread.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: dedication wins: contamination is invisible until it has scratched a day's work, so the inventory cost is paid up front and suspect wheels are quarantined, not cleaned by hope

conflict_axes.name: schedule_pressure_vs_safety_obligations
conflict_axes.description: Deadlines push toward unextracted quick passes, ungated new hires and chains held to the buff; the obligation classes at the station exist precisely for the moments they are inconvenient.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: safety and compliance beat throughput, cost and deadline - the program-wide dominance rule; a deadline never buys an exception at a spinning wheel

conflict_axes.name: customer_expectation_vs_honest_limits
conflict_axes.description: Customers hope finishing erases a piece's history; honesty requires naming what a budgeted, detail-preserving, porosity-aware finish cannot fix - and saying it before the work, not after.
poles: promise the transformation the customer imagines
disclose the limits the piece imposes
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the defect map conversation at intake is where expectations are set: remove, reduce and disclose classes agreed up front turn limits into professionalism instead of excuses

edge_cases.description: A chain or flexible-link bracelet arrives specified for pre-plate brightening
edge_cases.trigger: linked, flexible or wrappable goods appear in the finishing queue
edge_cases.mitigation: never at the wheel under any argument: route to steel-shot burnishing or hand methods; the catch-and-wrap hazard is the reason the routing rule is absolute

edge_cases.description: A zinc die-cast piece whose pits multiply as they are cut
edge_cases.trigger: pit count or size grows during cut-down on cast material
edge_cases.mitigation: stop at the recorded depth - the multiplication is the porosity diagnostic; photograph, flag the zone, and route to repair referral or leave-and-disclose via the customer

edge_cases.description: The hallmark sits in the middle of the one panel that needs leveling
edge_cases.trigger: a protected mark inside a mapped remove zone
edge_cases.mitigation: mask the mark and hand-level around it accepting a visible compromise, or obtain the documented sign-off for work over the mark; the mark is never silently sacrificed to the finish

edge_cases.description: A customer ring previously repaired with low-melt solder starts showing grey streaks under the buff
edge_cases.trigger: grey smear appearing near a joint during wheel work
edge_cases.mitigation: stop immediately, quarantine the wheel as lead-suspect, hand-finish the zone, flag it prominently on the traveler, and reset expectations with the customer about the repair's plating consequences

edge_cases.description: An antique gilt clock ornament suspected to be fire-gilt is brought in for a quick polish
edge_cases.trigger: antique ormolu-class goods reaching the finishing queue despite triage
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse bench work and refer to conservation: residual mercury in fire-gilt objects makes mechanical refinishing a recognized hazard class, and no sign-off path exists for it; escalate to triage that the piece slipped through

edge_cases.description: A gold-filled bangle arrives with deep scratches the customer wants gone
edge_cases.mitigation: burnish and disclose by default; explain that the skin is the product and cutting the scratches out spends it permanently - abrasive work only with the countersigned sign-off after that conversation

edge_cases.description: A hollow stamped piece flexes and oil-cans under wheel pressure
edge_cases.trigger: thin-walled hollow construction meeting normal cut-down force
edge_cases.mitigation: drop to light supported passes or reroute to burnishing; a dwelling or forceful wheel dents what it was meant to polish and can pop a seam by heat

edge_cases.description: The coloring mop begins leaving fine parallel scratches mid-shift
edge_cases.trigger: recurring scratch pattern appearing at the stage meant to remove none
edge_cases.mitigation: quarantine the mop at once, rake or retire it, audit the compound rack for a dedication breach, and re-inspect everything colored since the last clean QC pass

edge_cases.description: A partial refinish on a satin-finished piece will not match the untouched panels
edge_cases.trigger: sheen mismatch risk on a match-the-existing-texture job
edge_cases.mitigation: match direction and grade on a coupon against the reference before touching the piece; if no coupon matches, propose refinishing the whole visible face with customer agreement rather than delivering a mixed panel

edge_cases.description: Worn plate breaks through mid-buff on a job quoted as just brighten it
edge_cases.trigger: accidental breakthrough exposing base metal during light finishing
edge_cases.mitigation: stop and photograph immediately - do not blend the patch wider; re-contact the customer, because strip-and-replate versus accept-as-is is a new authorization, not a bench improvisation

edge_cases.description: Finished pieces sit for days before reaching the degrease line
edge_cases.trigger: a backlog or batching habit between finishing and chemistry
edge_cases.mitigation: route promptly as the default and note actual residue age on the traveler when delay happens, so the degrease line escalates its process instead of discovering hardened compound at the water-break stage

edge_cases.description: A mapped scratch turns out to be a dent as leveling proceeds
edge_cases.trigger: a defect that deepens rather than shrinks under correct technique
edge_cases.mitigation: stop - displaced metal cannot be sanded away, only surrounded; reclassify as a dent, disclose or refer for repair, and log the misread to sharpen future mapping

workflow.action: Verify the triage packet and sign-offs
workflow.description: Confirm substrate class, coating and joint flags, stone and organic clearance and any irreversibility sign-off before the piece enters the finishing queue
workflow.artifact: countersigned traveler accepted into the queue
workflow.gate: all required packet fields present; refuse/refer verdicts and missing sign-offs stop the job at intake

workflow.description: Agree finish class per face, texture direction and grade for non-mirror targets, and capture a reference sample on match jobs
workflow.artifact: finish spec recorded on the traveler with reference sample where applicable
workflow.gate: every face has a named finish class and match jobs carry a reference before any work

workflow.action: Map and class the defects under raking light
workflow.description: Survey all faces magnified under raking light; class every defect remove, reduce or disclose; photograph customer goods
workflow.artifact: defect map with classes and intake photographs
workflow.gate: every visible defect carries a class and every disclose item has customer acknowledgment

workflow.description: Name the thinnest irreplaceable layer (old plate, clad skin, wall, detail) and derive how much leveling the piece can survive
workflow.artifact: removal budget statement on the traveler
